# AI / Expert Quickstart

**Example status — excerpt:** blocks are terse API reminders. The tested
end-to-end contract is [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).

This is a compact map for readers who already know Python, PyTorch, and
Lightning. It summarizes the public path and links to the pages that own each
contract. For a runnable build-to-prediction example, use
[Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).

## Construct A Schema

Use top-level exports through `import relflow as rf`:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

import torch

import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model(
    name="order",
    d_model=64,
    n_layers=2,
    n_heads=4,
    batch_size=32,
    embed=True,
    optimizer=lambda module: torch.optim.AdamW(module.parameters(), lr=1e-3),
    customer_tier=rf.Category(size=16),
    line_items=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        sku=rf.Category(size=2048),
        quantity=rf.Number,
        price=rf.Number,
    ),
    returned=rf.Category(mask=True, size=2),
)

model
```

The generated root is named `record` unless `name=...` overrides it. A child
`Branch(length=...)` adds a repeated context. Only leaf tensorfields bind source
values; branches define model structure and alignment.

Configured `topk` values must be integers greater than 1 and strictly less than
Category `size`; binary categories therefore need no separate top-k list.
Category capacity counts content labels only—do not reserve an extra slot for
unavailable content.

## Match The Input Shape

The schema above reads records shaped like:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

record = {
    "customer_tier": "gold",
    "line_items": [
        {"sku": "ABC-123", "quantity": 2, "price": 19.99},
        {"sku": "XYZ-999", "quantity": 1, "price": 7.50},
    ],
    "returned": "false",
}
```

Arrow field names and nesting match the schema: `customer_tier` is a root field
and `sku` is a field on each `line_items` struct. This direct binding is the
default. Put an Arrow-native structural `query=...` on a root, branch, or leaf
when the source path differs; use an `@rf.preprocess` object for coordinated
reshaping, normalization, sorting, filtering, joins, or windowing.
See [Binding Data](core-concepts/binding-data.qmd) and
[Query Paths](core-concepts/querypaths.qmd).

## Assign Learning Roles

| Configuration | Input behavior | Output / learning behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain leaf | visible when present | context only by default |
| `mask=True` | always skipped by the encoder | supervised reconstruction |
| `mask=x` | sampled positions use a learned mask during training | context regularization only |
| `mask=rf.Mask(rate=x, reconstruct=True)` | sampled positions use a learned mask | reconstruction at selected positions |
| `mask=rf.Mask(query="selected", skip=True)` | selected positions are omitted from encoder work | train-only dropout by default |
| branch `mask=...` | one decision is shared by the entire selected branch coordinate | atomic subtree masking or skipping |
| `embed=True` | does not hide input | exports an embedding at the address |
| `active=False` | excluded from execution | remains in the serializable schema |

`mask=True` is shorthand for
`rf.Mask(skip=True, dropout=False, reconstruct=True)`. See
[Learning Modes & Embeddings](core-concepts/embeddings.qmd) for the canonical
role definitions and [Dynamic Masking](core-concepts/dynamic-masking.qmd) for
selection and branch atomicity. A policy with a remaining fractional `rate` is
inactive during ordinary prediction; use a deterministic Boolean selector for
request-time routing. See
[Dynamic Mask Preprocessors](guides/dynamic-mask-preprocessors.qmd) for complete
Arrow and Awkward selector recipes.

## Run The Lifecycle

RelFlow uses ordinary Lightning loops for training and large-batch prediction:

```python
import lightning.pytorch as lit
import pyarrow as pa

datamodule = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    train=train_table,
    validate=validate_table,
    num_workers=0,
    persistent_workers=False,
    pin_memory=False,
)

trainer = lit.Trainer(max_epochs=1)
trainer.fit(model=model, datamodule=datamodule)
metrics = trainer.validate(model=model, datamodule=datamodule)

model.save("model.pt")
restored = rf.Model.load("model.pt")

requests = validate_table.drop(["returned"]).slice(0, 1)
result = restored.predict(requests)
```

Prediction requests normally omit fields configured with `mask=True`.
`Model.predict` returns a `pyarrow.Table`; its `predictions` struct has one
field per schema address. Decoded leaves include `state`, type-specific
`content`, and `inferred`, while configured nodes can include `embedding`.

Use [Training With Lightning](guides/lightning.qmd) for trainer behavior,
[Data Modules](guides/data-modules.qmd) for ingestion, and
[Evaluation And Metrics](guides/evaluation.qmd) for model selection. Use
[Model Lifecycle](guides/model-lifecycle.qmd) for artifact and resume contracts,
and [Batch Inference](guides/batch-inference.qmd) for `rf.Writer` and
rank-partitioned Parquet output.

## Shape The Boundaries

A preprocessor is part of the Arrow input contract:

```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc

@rf.preprocess
def normalize_order(batch: rf.Batch) -> rf.Batch:
    tier = pc.utf8_lower(pc.utf8_trim_whitespace(batch.data["tier"]))
    data = pa.table(
        {
            "customer_tier": tier,
            "line_items": batch.data["items"],
        }
    )
    return batch.replace(data)
```

A postprocessor is part of the application output contract:

```python
@rf.postprocess
def response(batch: rf.Batch) -> rf.Batch:
    predictions = batch.data["predictions"]
    returned = pc.struct_field(predictions, "order/returned")
    content = pc.struct_field(returned, "content")
    return batch.replace(
        pa.table({"returned": pc.struct_field(content, "value")})
    )
```

Pass the same preprocessor through training and inference. Keep the stable,
typed model output intact until the postprocessor boundary. See
[Data Flow](core-concepts/data-flow.qmd) and
[Postprocessors](guides/postprocessors.qmd).

## Public API Map

| Need | Public surface | Authoritative page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root model | `rf.Model(...)` | [Model Tree](core-concepts/model-tree.qmd) |
| Repeated context | `rf.Branch(...)` | [Branch](data-types/branch.qmd) |
| Typed leaves | `rf.Number`, `Category`, `Cluster`, `Set`, `Hash`, `DateParts`, `Boolean`, `Vector`, `Text` | [Built-In Data Types](core-concepts/data-types.qmd) |
| Arrow input | `rf.ArrowDataModule` | [Data Modules](guides/data-modules.qmd) |
| Input adapters | `rf.PolarsDataModule`, `rf.CustomDataModule`, `rf.SyntheticDataModule` | [Data Modules](guides/data-modules.qmd) |
| Interactive prediction | `model.predict(...)` | [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd#interpret-the-prediction) |
| Prediction contract | Arrow `inputs` and address-named `predictions` structs | [Prediction Output](guides/prediction-output.qmd) |
| Batch prediction | `rf.Writer(...)` | [Batch Inference](guides/batch-inference.qmd) |
| Online prediction | `rf.Deployment(...)` | [Serving](guides/serving.qmd) |
| Input / output transforms | `@rf.preprocess`, `@rf.postprocess` | [Binding Data](core-concepts/binding-data.qmd), [Postprocessors](guides/postprocessors.qmd) |
| Schema selection / mutation | `rf.where(...)`, `update`, `extend`, `delete`, `reset`, `override` | [Model Tree](core-concepts/model-tree.qmd#schema-roles-and-mutations) |

## Contract Checklist

- Name the root with `Model(name=...)`; use child `Branch(length=...)` for
  repeated data.
- Keep `n_heads` positive and even. For the root, every Branch, and each leaf
  using `pooling="query"`, require `d_model % n_heads == 0` and
  `d_model // n_heads >= 2`.
- Use `Hash` for large identifiers whose equality matters. Matching values
  align across leaves in one encoded batch, though branch pooling can discard
  token-level correspondence.
- Use `Cluster` when a high-cardinality learned vocabulary should share a much
  smaller set of latent representations.
- Set bounded capacity for Category, Cluster, and Set fields, then monitor
  vocabulary growth rather than inventing a missing-value class.
- Use `overflow="tail"` only when source order places the newest values last.
- Include reconstruction values in train/validation data; prediction may omit
  only unconditional deterministic reconstructions such as `mask=True`.
- Preserve the same preprocessing, schema, vocabulary/normalizer state, and
  weights across evaluation and inference.
